moat_against: No pricing power — allowed ROE and cost recovery decided by KS/MO regulators; Kansas outcomes historically less constructive
Returns capped by design at the allowed ROE — no wide-moat compounder economics
$21.6B+ capex plan needs continuous external capital (debt + ATM equity); mild dilution and financing drag
Weather exposure and coal-fleet/environmental transition spend
Growth concentrated in a few data-center/industrial projects — delays or tougher rate treatment hit the plan directly
moat_for: Exclusive regulated service territory — no competitor can serve its Kansas/Missouri customers
Essential service with captive demand; load inflecting up on signed large-load contracts
~3.0 GW signed ESAs with 16–17-year minimum billing under LLPS tariffs — large customers pay premium rates and their share of system costs
Rate-base growth converts to earnings growth once assets enter rates (~12% guided rate-base CAGR)
moat_justification: Exclusive regulated KS/MO service territory with captive, essential demand and ~3.0 GW of signed large-load ESAs under premium LLPS tariffs — but pricing and returns are set by the KS/MO commissions, not the company, so the franchise yields allowed-ROE earnings, not pricing power; the $21.6B capex plan also needs continuous debt/ATM equity funding.
name: Evergy, Inc.
one_liner: Regulated KS/MO franchise, moat 5/10, with real regulated earnings growth (6–8%+ guided EPS, ~12% rate-base CAGR on signed data-center load) that the conservative OE screen structurally cannot credit — capex for rate base runs ~$3B/yr against ~$2B OCF, so OE is negative 0/5 years and no 15%-clearing price is computable; Tier F on the numbers, read with the utility-model caveat.
